newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat slips on rain but nearby May in squeeze.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat slips on rain but nearby May in squeeze.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures slipped slightly on Friday while the nearby May contract spiked with a strong gain on a supply squeeze.
May 1997 rose by A$5.50 to A$205.00 a tonne on four lots traded. Phil Lindsay of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures said the contract would expire soon and was experiencing a squeeze.
Other traded contracts slipped, with September 1997 and January 1998 both falling by 50 cents to A$200.00 and A$176.00 respectively.
Settlement prices were generally down in near-term months but slightly ahead in more distant months.
Lindsay said that good rain across most of the state had produced further selling interest in the Januuary contract.

The May 1997 price spike was accompanied by a A$5.00 a tonne increase in the Australian Wheat Board's cash bid prices to A$185.00 a tonne for current crop Australian Standard White delivered GrainCorp at Newcastle.
